title: What happens in the first 60 seconds after a rocket launches?
sources: NASA Kennedy Space Center Launch Trajectory

lines.text: What violent physics occurs in the first sixty seconds when a giant orbital rocket lifts off?
lines.caps: What happens in the *first | 60 seconds of a *launch?

lines.text: At liftoff, giant rocket engines consume thousands of gallons of liquid propellant every second.
lines.caps: Engines burn *thousands of gallons | of fuel every *second

lines.text: Giant water deluge trenches dump four hundred thousand gallons of water to dampen acoustic shockwaves.
lines.caps: Massive water trenches *suppress | acoustic shockwaves from *damage

lines.text: By second thirty, the rocket pushes past the speed of sound, creating a visible condensation shock cone.
At second sixty, the rocket hits Max Q, the point of maximum aerodynamic stress on the vehicle's frame.
lines.caps: Hits Max Q: the most *violent | structural stress of *flight!

lines.text: Rushing through thick atmosphere at two thousand miles per hour, engines throttle down to prevent ripping apart.
Surviving those first sixty seconds is the hardest physical hurdle of reaching outer space.
